```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

H1: Respondents with doctoral or equivalent professional degrees will have lower relationship qualilty (measured with warmth, understanding, magic, and passion) in their relationships. 

H2: Male respondents who spend a lot of time grooming their hair daily will also report a lot of time spent on social media daily. 

## Load package and data

```{r load, message=FALSE}
# load the codeook package

library(codebook)

#load data

###JK: The input file is inside the raw folder in your submitted project. ###
# Replace the line below with:
# raw <- read.csv("raw/data_doctored.csv")
###  End of comment ###

raw <- read.csv("data_doctored.csv")

# check row and column counts and inspect the first few rows

dim(raw)
str(raw)


# make data with ID, level of education, perceived warm, perceived understanding, percieved magic, perceived passion, time spent grooming hair, and time spent on social media 

data <- raw[,c("ResponseId","cot_educ", "Relationship_status", "Love_1","Love_5","Love_9","Love_10", "Time_A_hair_1","Time_social_media_1", "Sex_birth")]

dim(data)
str(data)

```


## 2. Check participant IDs

```{r participantIds}

#count nas, blanks, and duplicates

summary(data$ResponseId)

#inspect records with missing or blank IDs

missingID <- which(is.na(data$ResponseId))
print(data[missingID,])

#remove the known empty record with no ID, then check the row count
data <- data[!is.na(data$ResponseId),]

```

## 3. Recode level of education

```{r levelEducation}
# codebook: 1=None; 2=Primary; 3=Secondary; 4=High school/technical college; 5=Bachelor; 6=Master; 7=PhD/MD/JD or equivalent

table(data$cot_educ,useNA="ifany")

#turn Sex_birth into a factor with labels Male, Female, and Intersex

data$cot_educ <- factor(data$cot_educ,
                         levels = c(1,2,3,4,
                                    5,6,7),
                         labels = 
c("None", "Primary", "Secondary", "HighSchoolorTech", "Bachelor", "Master", "PhDorEq"))

#check to see if it worked

table(data$cot_educ,useNA="ifany")


```

## 4. Validate relative love
```{r loveVars}
#group 4 chosen love variables

###JK: Consider using relationship satisfaction (prqc_1-3) for H1 instead. ###
# These items assess satisfaction, contentment, and happiness with the relationship, which may fit your hypothesis better than selected intimacy and passion items.
# You could average the three items (1-7, no reverse coding), focus on participants in relationships (statuses 1, 2, and 3), and describe H1 as predicting relationship satisfaction.
# If you want to use Love items, I recommend using all Love items.
# Love_1 and Love_5 come from intimacy, while Love_9 and Love_10 come from passion.
# Summing these four selected items does not make a validated overall relationship-quality score.
# Use a complete subscale from the codebook and update the variables selected from raw accordingly.
###  End of comment ###

loveVars <- c("Love_1","Love_5","Love_9","Love_10")

#see summary of variables

summary(data[,loveVars])

#count NAs

colSums(is.na(data[loveVars]))

#calculate total score; leave the total NA if any item is missing

data$loveTotal <- 
rowSums(data[,loveVars],na.rm=FALSE)
summary(data$loveTotal)

#check that each observed score is between 1 and 5

data$loveRange <- rowSums(
  data[,loveVars] < 1 | data[,loveVars] > 5,
  na.rm=TRUE
) == FALSE

#define loveValid: total present and each item in range

data$loveValid <- !is.na(data$loveTotal) 
table(data$loveValid)

###JK: Your H1 table currently keeps Love_10 alone instead of the composite you calculated. ###
# loveTotal is calculated above but omitted from h1Data, so the final table and codebook use only the single passion item.
# Also, loveRange is checked but never used when selecting valid rows.
# After deciding on your Love items above, replace the h1Data assignment below with:
# h1Data <- data[
#   data$loveValid & data$loveRange & !is.na(data$cot_educ),
#   c("ResponseId", "cot_educ", "loveTotal")
# ]
# Replace the later range(h1Data$Love_10) check with range(h1Data$loveTotal).
# Your hypothesis compares doctoral/professional degree holders with others, while cot_educ currently retains all seven education categories.
# To create the two groups explicitly, add this after creating h1Data:
# h1Data$degree_group <- factor(ifelse(h1Data$cot_educ == "PhDorEq", "Doctoral/professional", "Other education"))
# table(h1Data$degree_group)
###  End of comment ###

#make h1Data with ID, cot_educ and preference_imp_physat
h1Data <- data[data$loveValid & ! is.na(data$cot_educ),c("ResponseId","cot_educ","Love_10")]


```


## 5. Hair grooming & social media time 
```{r hairSocial}
#recode Sex_Birth
table(data$Sex_birth,useNA="ifany")

#turn Sex_birth into a factor with labels Male, Female, and Intersex
data$Sex_birth <- factor(data$Sex_birth,
                         levels = c(0,1,2),
                         labels = c("Male","Female","Intersex"))

###JK: H2 specifies male respondents, but this selection includes both males and females. ###
# Replace the line below with:
# sexData <- data[data$Sex_birth == "Male" & !is.na(data$Sex_birth), ]
###  End of comment ###

sexData <- data[data$Sex_birth %in% c("Male", "Female"),]

#define the items to check, both use 0-360 minutes

minutes <- c("Time_social_media_1","Time_A_hair_1")

#check the summaries and missing responses

summary(sexData[,minutes])
colSums(is.na(sexData[,minutes]))

#inspect the response frequencies for each item

for(i in minutes){
  print(i)
  print(table(sexData[,i],useNA="ifany"))
}

###JK: These are time measurements from 0 to 360 minutes, not 1-7 ratings. ###
# The loop below keeps only 1-7 minutes and changes valid values such as 0, 30, and 120 to NA.
# Replace the loop below with:
# for(i in minutes){
#   sexData[,i] <- ifelse(sexData[,i] >= 0 & sexData[,i] <= 360, sexData[,i], NA)
# }
# After correcting the male-only selection above, replace the h2Data assignment with:
# h2Data <- sexData[
#   !is.na(sexData$Time_social_media_1) & !is.na(sexData$Time_A_hair_1),
#   c("ResponseId", "Sex_birth", "Time_A_hair_1", "Time_social_media_1")
# ]
# This keeps the H2 variables without carrying unrelated education and Love columns into the final table.
# Update the later H2 range-check comment to 0-360 rather than 1-7.
###  End of comment ###

#replace any codes outside 0-360 with NA
for(i in minutes){
  sexData[,i] <- ifelse(sexData[,i] %in% 1:7,sexData[,i],NA)
}

#make h2Data with sex, hair time, and social media time 
h2Data <- sexData[!is.na(sexData$Time_social_media_1) & !is.na(sexData$Time_A_hair_1),]
```

## 7. Check the final tables

```{r final_tables}
#check rows, columns, types, and missing values in h1Data
#one row per participant, one column per variable
dim(h1Data)
str(h1Data)
head(h1Data)
colSums(is.na(h1Data))
table(h1Data$cot_educ,useNA="ifany")
range(h1Data$Love_10)
sum(duplicated(h1Data$ResponseId))

#repeat the checks for h2Data; both scores should be within 1-7
dim(h2Data)
str(h2Data)
head(h2Data)
colSums(is.na(h2Data))
range(h2Data$Time_social_media_1)
range(h2Data$Time_A_hair_1)
sum(duplicated(h2Data$ResponseId))
```

## 8. Add labels and generate codebooks

The descriptions come from the original codebook and our scoring decisions.
`compact_codebook()` adds summaries from the actual data. Knit the Rmd to
display the formatted codebooks.
H1 includes participants with an ID, a valid sex-at-birth category, and six
allocations between 0 and 30 that total 30. Factor level numbers in the
generated table are internal R positions, not the original survey codes.

```{r h1_codebook}
###JK: Add variable descriptions with var_label() before generating the codebooks, following Section 8 of my Lab03 example. ###
# Include the education-group definition, selected composite items, scoring range, missing-data rule, and what higher scores mean for H1.
# Replace the inclusion descriptions above and below with your own rules; the 30-point allocation, qoa, commitment, and relationship-status statements are left over from the example.
###  End of comment ###

#generate the h1Data codebook
compact_codebook(h1Data)

```

H2 includes participants with an ID, relationship status 1, 2, or 3, and
valid nonmissing qoa and at least one valid commitment response.

```{r h2_codebook}
#generate the h2Data codebook
compact_codebook(h2Data)

```

## 9. Save the final tables

```{r save}
#create data/processed_data if needed
dir.create("data/processed_data",recursive=T,showWarnings=F)

#save h1Data and h2Data without an extra row-number column
write.csv(h1Data,"data/processed_data/practice_h1.csv",row.names=F)
write.csv(h2Data,"data/processed_data/practice_h2.csv",row.names=F)

#read the files back and confirm their dimensions
h1Saved <- read.csv("data/processed_data/practice_h1.csv")
h2Saved <- read.csv("data/processed_data/practice_h2.csv")
dim(h1Saved)
dim(h2Saved)

```
